paper.title: Associations of age, occupation and nationality of seafarers with risk of evacuations at sea: a register-based study on Danish-flagged merchant ships
paper.code_data_availability: No data or code availability statement. On data handling the paper says only: …

registers.name_in_paper: the Telemedical Assistance Service (TMAS) of Denmark, i.e. Radio Medical Denmark (RMD)
registers.role: outcomes (evacuation cases) and the demographic characteristics of the cases
variables_mentioned: diagnoses coded according to the International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision (ICD-10)
sea location of the evacuation (recorded for only 37% of cases)
name of the shipping company (recorded for only 41% of evacuations)

registers.name_in_paper: the annual record of seafarers on board ships registered in the Danish Registers of Shipping, which is administered by the Danish Maritime Authority (DMA)
registers.role: sample frame / population at risk (denominator for incidence rates)

linkages: The two sources are combined at the level of the demographic categories, not of persons: 'We combined these data sources to calculate adjusted incidence rates and to perform analyses on the association between explanatory variables and outcomes'; 'the characteristics from RMD had to match those from the DMA'.
Seafarers on Danish-flagged ships are 'regardless of their nationality or place of residence, registered in the Danish International Register of Shipping'.

sample.universe: Seafarers on board Danish-flagged merchant ships registered in the Danish Registers of Shipping (Danish International Register of Shipping), 2004-2014, regardless of nationality or place of residence
sample.unit_of_observation: Seafarer, classified as an evacuated case or a noncase; annual seafarer counts serve as person-years for the incidence rates
selection_rules: Evacuations ascertained from TMAS/RMD contacts; 'All of the cases in this study were cases where an evacuation had taken place'; a ship advised to divert to the nearest port of call, or already in port, is not a medevac
Only evacuations from the merchant fleet included: the DMA data have no data on fishermen and very limited information on ferries
Study period 2004 through 2014, 'determined by the availability and the quality of data'

construction_notes: Evacuations grouped by ICD-10 into four mutually exclusive categories: circulatory I00-I99; digestive K00-K93; injury, poisoning and other external causes S00-T98; all other causes incl. R00-R99
Age grouped into three categories: under 30, 30-49, and 50 years and over (reference 30-49)
Nationality in three categories: Danish citizens, non-Danish EU, non-EU; 'EU indicates here the European Union but also the member countries of the European Economic Area and Switzerland'

Occupation classified into deck officers, engine officers and non-officers; deck and engine officers combined into one officer category because the DMA population-at-risk data did not encompass the age distribution for these officer groups separately
Rates are per 1,000 person-years and derived from logistic models; age-adjusted incidence rates obtained as adjusted marginal means with 95% CIs
Characteristics of noncases and cases compared with Chi square tests (Table 1)
All analyses conducted in Stata version 16

claims.statement: Among officers in the Danish-flagged merchant fleet 2004-2014, seafarers aged under 30 years (vs 30-49) had no statistically significant difference in odds of evacuation from all causes (unadjusted odds ratio 0.96, 95% CI 0.48-1.93).

register_source.value: Danish Maritime Authority (DMA) annual record of seafarers on board ships registered in the Danish Registers of Shipping for the population at risk, and TMAS/Radio Medical Denmark records for the evacuated cases. Not a Statistics Denmark register; no DST register code or variable name is given.

definition.value: Indicator for the youngest of three age categories - 'age was grouped into three categories: under 30 years, from 30 to 49 years, and 50 years and over' - contrasted with the reference category 30-49 years.

timing.value: Measured contemporaneously with the outcome: demographic characteristics as recorded in the annual DMA record of seafarers on Danish-flagged merchant ships (population at risk) and in the TMAS/RMD record at the time of the evacuation, 2004-2014. No information on actual time on board.

outcome.label: Evacuation from all causes (evacuated case vs noncase)

register_source.value: Telemedical Assistance Service (TMAS) of Denmark / Radio Medical Denmark (RMD) records of evacuations; 'All reports from TMAS include diagnoses coded according to the International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision (ICD-10)'. Not a Statistics Denmark register; no DST register code or variable name is given.

definition.value: Binary indicator of having been medically evacuated at sea during 2004-2014, from TMAS/RMD records: 'A medical evacuation is often referred to as a medevac. This usually means an acute rescue using helicopter, but it can also include using fast rescue boats'. Diversion of the ship to the nearest port of call, or a ship already in port, is not counted as a medevac. Used as the dependent variable of a logistic regression (403 cases vs 72,941 noncases).

timing.value: Evacuations reported to the TMAS during the 11-year study period 2004-2014; measured as case status at the end of the period, contemporaneously with the demographic characteristics.

units.value: odds ratio (odds of being an evacuated case rather than a noncase, relative to the reference category)

estimand.target_population: Seafarers on Danish-flagged merchant ships 2004-2014, officers only

population.description: Seafarers in the Danish-flagged merchant fleet 2004-2014 (403 evacuated cases and 72,941 noncases, N=73,344); officers only
population.ages: working ages, grouped <30, 30-49 and 50 years or over
subgroups_defined: occupational position: deck officers, engine officers, non-officers (officers combined)
nationality: Danish, EU non-Danish (incl. EEA and Switzerland), non-EU
population.selection: Seafarers appearing in the annual DMA record of seafarers on ships registered in the Danish Registers of Shipping (merchant fleet only; fishermen excluded and ferries excluded for lack of data); evacuation cases ascertained from TMAS/RMD contacts

identification.source_of_variation: None exogenous: a cross-sectional comparison of case/noncase status across demographic groups within an 11-year register-based cohort of seafarers. The paper calls the estimates associations.

key_assumptions.assumption: The annual DMA record of the number of seafarers measures the population at risk, even though actual time on board is unknown; this does not distort the associations.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated as a limitation and argued away in words only: 'It is, however, improbable that this would have affected relations between explanatory variables and outcomes.'

key_assumptions.assumption: Evacuation cases from the TMAS/RMD records and the DMA counts of seafarers refer to the same underlying population and can be matched on the broad categories of age, occupational position and nationality.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The Methods state that 'the characteristics from RMD had to match those from the DMA' and that the two sources were combined; the paper also notes that only 41% of evacuations recorded the shipping company, of which 91% were Danish-flagged.

key_assumptions.assumption: No covariate adjustment is made for this contrast; the odds ratio is reported as an unadjusted association.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Table 2 note 'Model 1: Unadjusted' and the Methods: 'we used unadjusted models for the associations between age, occupation and nationality, and evacuations from all causes'.

key_assumptions.assumption: Analysis is conditioned on being a seafarer in the Danish-flagged merchant fleet; fishermen and ferries are excluded from the data.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Methods: the DMA data have no data on fishermen and very limited information on ferries, so 'we included only evacuations from the merchant fleet in our analysis'.

implies_edges.from: Employment in the Danish-flagged merchant fleet
implies_edges.to: Evacuation from all causes (evacuated case vs noncase)

key_assumptions.assumption: The odds ratio from the case/noncase logistic model can be read as a ratio of risks ('an elevated risk for evacuations with an odds ratio of ...').

threats_discussed: The population at risk is an annual record of the number of seafarers, so actual time on board is unknown and incidence rates 'may thus be under- or overestimated'

23% of all evacuations were coded to ICD-10 R00-R99 ('Symptoms, sign and abnormal clinical and laboratory findings, not elsewhere classified'), so rates in the three specific cause categories may be underestimates
Only 37% of cases had a record of the sea location, so location could not be used as a confounder

Only 41% of evacuations recorded the shipping company (91% of those Danish-flagged), so some cases may come from foreign-flagged ships not in the denominator; 'our incident rates are likely overestimated'
Differences in evacuation incidence 'may also result from differences in reporting or underreporting'
'one might also ask if one group is preferred to another when deciding whether to evacuate or not'
robustness_checks: Interaction terms for age x occupation and nationality x occupation were fitted; 'As the interaction was present, we fitted these analyses separately for officers and non-officers'
unresolved_confounders: Sea location of the evacuation: 'As only 37% of the cases had a record of the location, we were not able to use the location as a confounder.'
Actual time on board / person-time at risk, unknown because the denominator is an annual headcount
Differential reporting or underreporting of illness and injury, possibly related to nationality and type or length of employment contract

Lifestyle and occupational risk factors (diet, obesity, exercise, smoking, noise, chemical exposure): 'it is presently unclear whether there are differences in the prevalence of these risk factors between officers and non-officers'
The set of adjustable covariates itself: 'The type of data on the population at risk was also the reason why the number of explanatory or confounding variables was limited.'

estimator.value: logistic regression (logit), reported as odds ratios; Stata 16

estimation.specification: Table 2, Officers panel, Model 1: unadjusted logistic regression of evacuation (case vs noncase) on age group (reference 30-49 years), fitted separately for officers

sample_n.value: 73 evacuation cases among officers (Table 2 'Total' row); the number of officer noncases entering the model is not printed (study population N=73,344 with 403 cases and 72,941 noncases)

source_table.value: Table 2, Officers panel, Model 1, row 'Age group under 30 years (versus 30-49 years)'

heterogeneity.dimension: Occupational position (officers vs non-officers)
heterogeneity.finding: Interaction terms for age and occupation and for nationality and occupation were fitted; 'As the interaction was present, we fitted these analyses separately for officers and non-officers'. No interaction estimate or test statistic is reported.

ambiguities: Page numbers in this record are 1-based PDF page indices of paper.pdf (Table 2 on PDF page 22, Table 3 on PDF page 23); the digest cites the printed manuscript page labels (21 and 22), which are one less than the PDF index.

baseline_mean is the reference-category age-adjusted rate per 1,000 person-years printed in the 'Rate' column of the source table, not the mean of the binary case/noncase regression outcome, which the paper does not print.

The paper frames every estimate as an association (title: 'Associations of age, occupation and nationality of seafarers with risk of evacuations at sea'; 'The present observational results suggest'), so identification.strategy is recorded as descriptive and the graph edge kind causal_tested should be read as 'this pair was examined and a difference was found', not as a causal effect the authors claim.

evidence.how: Read the 'Rate' column of the reference category of this contrast in the source table (rate per 1,000 person-years, derived by the authors from the logistic models) and recorded it as the baseline level of the outcome; no mean of the binary case/noncase outcome is printed.

value.claimed_domain: Seafarers on Danish-flagged merchant ships; the authors explicitly limit the domain, stating that the findings 'are not necessarily generalizable to merchant fleets from other countries' and that 'Future research covering other countries is thus needed to confirm our observations'.
boundary_conditions: Danish-flagged merchant fleet only (fishermen and ferries excluded)
Safety standards and telemedicine services vary across countries, so results may not transfer

ambiguities: Page numbers in this record are 1-based PDF page indices of paper.pdf (Table 2 on PDF page 22, Table 3 on PDF page 23); the digest cites the printed manuscript page labels (21 and 22), which are one less than the PDF index.

baseline_mean is the reference-category age-adjusted rate per 1,000 person-years printed in the 'Rate' column of the source table, not the mean of the binary case/noncase regression outcome, which the paper does not print.

The paper frames every estimate as an association (title: 'Associations of age, occupation and nationality of seafarers with risk of evacuations at sea'; 'The present observational results suggest'), so identification.strategy is recorded as descriptive and the graph edge kind causal_tested should be read as 'this pair was examined and a difference was found', not as a causal effect the authors claim.

evidence.how: Read the 'Rate' column of the reference category of this contrast in the source table (rate per 1,000 person-years, derived by the authors from the logistic models) and recorded it as the baseline level of the outcome; no mean of the binary case/noncase outcome is printed.

value.claimed_domain: Seafarers on Danish-flagged merchant ships; the authors explicitly limit the domain, stating that the findings 'are not necessarily generalizable to merchant fleets from other countries' and that 'Future research covering other countries is thus needed to confirm our observations'.
boundary_conditions: Danish-flagged merchant fleet only (fishermen and ferries excluded)
Safety standards and telemedicine services vary across countries, so results may not transfer

outcomes_examined_not_reported: Annual numbers of evacuations 2004-2014: 'there was a large variation in the number of evacuations: from 57 cases in 2004 to 22 cases in 2014 (data not shown)'
Estimates or test statistics for the fitted age x occupation and nationality x occupation interaction terms; only 'As the interaction was present' is reported
Separate estimates for deck officers and engine officers, which were combined because the DMA population-at-risk data lacked their age distribution

anchor_quote.text: Table 2. Odds ratios and accompanying 95% confidence intervals for the association between age and nationality and evacuations from all causes among officers and non-officers in 2004-2014.

claims.statement: Among officers in the Danish-flagged merchant fleet 2004-2014, seafarers from non-EU countries (vs Danish) had no statistically significant difference in odds of evacuation from all causes (unadjusted odds ratio 0.99, 95% CI 0.59-1.65).

register_source.value: Danish Maritime Authority (DMA) annual record of seafarers on board ships registered in the Danish Registers of Shipping for the population at risk, and TMAS/Radio Medical Denmark records for the evacuated cases. Not a Statistics Denmark register; no DST register code or variable name is given.

definition.value: Indicator for the category 'Non-EU' of a three-category nationality classification (Danish citizens; non-Danish European Union countries; non-European Union citizens), contrasted with Danish citizens.

timing.value: Measured contemporaneously with the outcome: demographic characteristics as recorded in the annual DMA record of seafarers on Danish-flagged merchant ships (population at risk) and in the TMAS/RMD record at the time of the evacuation, 2004-2014. No information on actual time on board.

outcome.label: Evacuation from all causes (evacuated case vs noncase)

register_source.value: Telemedical Assistance Service (TMAS) of Denmark / Radio Medical Denmark (RMD) records of evacuations; 'All reports from TMAS include diagnoses coded according to the International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision (ICD-10)'. Not a Statistics Denmark register; no DST register code or variable name is given.

definition.value: Binary indicator of having been medically evacuated at sea during 2004-2014, from TMAS/RMD records: 'A medical evacuation is often referred to as a medevac. This usually means an acute rescue using helicopter, but it can also include using fast rescue boats'. Diversion of the ship to the nearest port of call, or a ship already in port, is not counted as a medevac. Used as the dependent variable of a logistic regression (403 cases vs 72,941 noncases).

timing.value: Evacuations reported to the TMAS during the 11-year study period 2004-2014; measured as case status at the end of the period, contemporaneously with the demographic characteristics.

units.value: odds ratio (odds of being an evacuated case rather than a noncase, relative to the reference category)

estimand.target_population: Seafarers on Danish-flagged merchant ships 2004-2014, officers only

population.description: Seafarers in the Danish-flagged merchant fleet 2004-2014 (403 evacuated cases and 72,941 noncases, N=73,344); officers only
population.ages: working ages, grouped <30, 30-49 and 50 years or over
subgroups_defined: occupational position: deck officers, engine officers, non-officers (officers combined)
nationality: Danish, EU non-Danish (incl. EEA and Switzerland), non-EU
population.selection: Seafarers appearing in the annual DMA record of seafarers on ships registered in the Danish Registers of Shipping (merchant fleet only; fishermen excluded and ferries excluded for lack of data); evacuation cases ascertained from TMAS/RMD contacts

identification.source_of_variation: None exogenous: a cross-sectional comparison of case/noncase status across demographic groups within an 11-year register-based cohort of seafarers. The paper calls the estimates associations.

key_assumptions.assumption: The annual DMA record of the number of seafarers measures the population at risk, even though actual time on board is unknown; this does not distort the associations.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated as a limitation and argued away in words only: 'It is, however, improbable that this would have affected relations between explanatory variables and outcomes.'

key_assumptions.assumption: Evacuation cases from the TMAS/RMD records and the DMA counts of seafarers refer to the same underlying population and can be matched on the broad categories of age, occupational position and nationality.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The Methods state that 'the characteristics from RMD had to match those from the DMA' and that the two sources were combined; the paper also notes that only 41% of evacuations recorded the shipping company, of which 91% were Danish-flagged.

key_assumptions.assumption: No covariate adjustment is made for this contrast; the odds ratio is reported as an unadjusted association.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Table 2 note 'Model 1: Unadjusted' and the Methods: 'we used unadjusted models for the associations between age, occupation and nationality, and evacuations from all causes'.

key_assumptions.assumption: Analysis is conditioned on being a seafarer in the Danish-flagged merchant fleet; fishermen and ferries are excluded from the data.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Methods: the DMA data have no data on fishermen and very limited information on ferries, so 'we included only evacuations from the merchant fleet in our analysis'.

implies_edges.from: Employment in the Danish-flagged merchant fleet
implies_edges.to: Evacuation from all causes (evacuated case vs noncase)

key_assumptions.assumption: The odds ratio from the case/noncase logistic model can be read as a ratio of risks ('an elevated risk for evacuations with an odds ratio of ...').
Reporting of illness and injury to the TMAS, and the decision to evacuate, do not depend on the seafarer's nationality or occupational position.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Raised and NOT resolved: the paper states that differences 'may also result from differences in reporting or underreporting', cites evidence of fewer reports by foreign seafarers, and asserts only that TMAS decisions 'are made objectively'.

implies_edges.from: Nationality
implies_edges.to: Reporting of illness or injury to the Telemedical Assistance Service

threats_discussed: The population at risk is an annual record of the number of seafarers, so actual time on board is unknown and incidence rates 'may thus be under- or overestimated'

23% of all evacuations were coded to ICD-10 R00-R99 ('Symptoms, sign and abnormal clinical and laboratory findings, not elsewhere classified'), so rates in the three specific cause categories may be underestimates
Only 37% of cases had a record of the sea location, so location could not be used as a confounder

Only 41% of evacuations recorded the shipping company (91% of those Danish-flagged), so some cases may come from foreign-flagged ships not in the denominator; 'our incident rates are likely overestimated'
Differences in evacuation incidence 'may also result from differences in reporting or underreporting'
'one might also ask if one group is preferred to another when deciding whether to evacuate or not'
robustness_checks: Interaction terms for age x occupation and nationality x occupation were fitted; 'As the interaction was present, we fitted these analyses separately for officers and non-officers'

Additional analysis of the country composition of evacuations among non-Danish EU seafarers (Polish seafarers 32% of those evacuations), though 'we have no information on the country-level distribution of the population at risk'
unresolved_confounders: Sea location of the evacuation: 'As only 37% of the cases had a record of the location, we were not able to use the location as a confounder.'
Actual time on board / person-time at risk, unknown because the denominator is an annual headcount
Differential reporting or underreporting of illness and injury, possibly related to nationality and type or length of employment contract

Lifestyle and occupational risk factors (diet, obesity, exercise, smoking, noise, chemical exposure): 'it is presently unclear whether there are differences in the prevalence of these risk factors between officers and non-officers'
The set of adjustable covariates itself: 'The type of data on the population at risk was also the reason why the number of explanatory or confounding variables was limited.'

estimator.value: logistic regression (logit), reported as odds ratios; Stata 16

estimation.specification: Table 2, Officers panel, Model 1: unadjusted logistic regression of evacuation (case vs noncase) on nationality (reference Danish), fitted separately for officers

sample_n.value: 73 evacuation cases among officers (Table 2 'Total' row); the number of officer noncases entering the model is not printed (study population N=73,344 with 403 cases and 72,941 noncases)

source_table.value: Table 2, Officers panel, Model 1, row 'Nationality: non-European Union country (versus Danish)'

heterogeneity.dimension: Occupational position (officers vs non-officers)
heterogeneity.finding: Interaction terms for age and occupation and for nationality and occupation were fitted; 'As the interaction was present, we fitted these analyses separately for officers and non-officers'. No interaction estimate or test statistic is reported.
